description.para: The following constants map to the XPAR parameters created in the xparameters.h file.
They are defined here so that all the needed parameters can be easily changed in one place.
The following constants define the positions of the buttons and LEDs in each channel of the GPIO.
The following constants define the GPIO channel that is used for the buttons and the LEDs.
They allow the channels to be reversed easily.

detaileddescription.para: The following constant determines which buttons must be pressed at the same time to cause interrupt processing to stop and start.
The following constant is used to wait after an LED is turned on to make sure that it is visible to the human eye. This constant might need to be tuned for faster or slower processor speeds.

briefdescription.para: Holds the global GPIO driver instance.

detaileddescription.para: The instance is declared globally so it is zeroed and easily accessible from a debugger.

briefdescription.para: GPIO channel mask that is needed by the interrupt handler.

detaileddescription.para: This is the entry function from the TestAppGen tool generated application, which tests the interrupts when enabled in the GPIO.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the GPIO driver instance.
Pointer where the data read from the GPIO input is returned.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the test is successful.
XST_FAILURE if the test is not successful.

simplesect.para: In XSCT/classic flow, DeviceId is used to look up the device configuration.

detaileddescription.para: This is the main function of the GPIO example. It is responsible for initializing the GPIO device, setting up interrupts, and providing a foreground loop so that interrupts can occur in the background.

briefdescription.para: Demonstrates usage of the GPIO driver (XGpio) in interrupt-driven mode.

detaileddescription.para: This file contains a design example using the GPIO driver (XGpio) in an interrupt-driven mode of operation. This example assumes that there is an interrupt controller in the hardware system and the GPIO device is connected to the interrupt controller.
This file is used in the Peripheral Tests Application in SDK to include a simplified test for GPIO interrupts.
The buttons and LEDs are on two separate channels of the GPIO. This separation prevents interrupts when the LEDs turn on and off.
